dossier.valuation_method: Warranted price-to-book [(ROE-g)/(CoE-g)] on a loan-level-derived economic book value with a derived bottom-up normalized-ROE bridge, probability-weighted across three credit-resolution scenarios (composite of excess-returns branches); cross-checked vs. a probability-weighted dividend-discount model (~$4.3-$5.3) and CRE-mREIT peer P/B (~$4.9)
dossier.thesis_summary: ACRE is a sub-scale, externally-managed senior CRE mortgage REIT in turnaround, valued on the credibility of its ~$8.90 common book (pre-CECL $11.39; $138.3M/768bps reserve already taken) and the through-cycle ROE it can earn on it. Its two non-accruals are already carried at a ~35% markdown (~$170M net vs ~$261M gross), with the more-impaired Chicago office (90%+ occupied, positive NCF) more heavily reserved; residual risk is the lighter-reserved Brooklyn condo sellout plus a dividend funded from capital. A derived normalized ROE of ~7-8% (capped by thin spreads, ~3% sub-scale G&A and the 1.5% base fee) on a derived economic book yields warranted P/B ~0.54x -> FMV ~$4.77, with a firm ~$7 economic-NAV floor and ~30% upside if the two loans resolve cleanly.
key_value_drivers: Brooklyn condo sellout outcome (lighter-reserved, asymmetric, ~65-70% LGD-given-loss if it fails; specific reserve not separately disclosed)
Chicago office resolution vs its conservative mark (more-impaired but heavier-reserved within the ~$91M two-loan reserve / ~35% combined markdown)
Derived normalized ROE (6-9%) vs systematic cost of equity (~12.8%), structurally capped by thin senior spreads + ~3% sub-scale G&A + 1.5% base fee
Dividend coverage by distributable earnings (currently uncovered; ~100% of 2025 book decline was the dividend, not credit)
Re-levering 1.9x -> ~3x and redeploying ~$170M of zero-yielding non-accruals into SOFR+2.25-2.75% loans
key_risks: Brooklyn condo sellout shortfall / forced bulk sale (lighter-reserved, asymmetric)
Chicago office clears below its mark
Distributable EPS keeps missing the $0.15 quarterly dividend -> third cut
External-management 1.5% base fee drag plus 20%-over-8%-hurdle incentive skim capping upside
Recourse, mark-to-market repo (~$1.18B): a ~10% collateral markdown implies ~$118M margin calls vs liquidity that fell to ~$101M by early May 2026 -> would exceed liquidity in a severe shock
Lower SOFR compressing absolute net interest income
what_would_change_my_mind: Chicago and Brooklyn resolved within ~10% of marks (-> ~$6+)
Two consecutive quarters of distributable EPS covering the $0.15 dividend
A further large CECL build or new risk-4/5 migration (-> ~$3)
A third dividend cut, confirming the grind/deterioration path

judge_gaps: The central two-way variable — Brooklyn condo's specific CECL reserve and likely loss-given-sellout — remains unquantified (honestly flagged as undisclosed); a best-in-existence report would extract or tightly bound it from the 10-Q's loan-by-loan/Schedule IV CECL detail or fair-value disclosures, since the entire edge hinges on it

The '~$170M net / ~$261M gross / ~35% markdown' anchor carries minor ambiguity over whether management's $170M-net figure covers exactly the two loans or all non-accruals; a definitive reconciliation of each loan's amortized cost vs specific allowance would remove it

ROE bridge uses a 1.5%-of-GAAP-equity base fee (~$7.2M) versus the ~1.9% effective run-rate (~$9.6M) implied by the management agreement's equity definition — understating fee drag and modestly overstating derived ROE
A few CECL-trend figures in the multi-year table are approximate (~$110M FY2023, ~$145M FY2024) rather than pulled exactly

The conclusion is a measured 'fairly valued / pass unless <$4.40' — sound and well-supported, but a modest mispricing edge rather than a differentiated, high-conviction call, which inherently limits its actionable upside
